note: Authored replay trace. The drafts are hand-written to exercise the validator's four most load-bearing checks — value-denominated earn caps, exclusivity groups, unpriceable protections and provenance — and every recorded verdict was produced by running that draft through plumbline.authoring.validate_draft for real. Replay re-validates rather than trusting these verdicts. Overwrite with a genuine claude-opus-5 transcript via `python -m agent.author --terms meridian_vantage --live --record`.
narration: Reading the terms. Sections 2.1 and 2.2 are earn multipliers, 3.1-3.3 are statement credits with stated remaining balances, 5.1-5.2 are protections and 6.1 is a service. Section 2.3 gives the point value, so I can convert the multipliers to basis points.
Drafting: 4 points per dollar at 1 cent each is 400 bp, 3 points per dollar is 300 bp. Submitting.

Rejected, and the codes are fair. The $50,000 dining cap is a SPEND figure and I put it in the value slot, which would have overstated that benefit by 25x. Section 3.4 says the dining credit and the restaurant week credit cannot both apply to one transaction, so both belong in the exclusivity group, not just one. Trip delay states no amount, so it cannot be a priced protection. And I left a provenance placeholder on the streaming credit.
Revised: capacity 200000 ($50,000 of qualifying spend at 400 bp), both dining credits in dining_line, trip delay declared unpriced, streaming provenance cited. Resubmitting.
Accepted. The Meridian Vantage Card manifest declares 8 benefits, 5 of them priced.
